title: Virtualized decimation profiles and announceable thresholds for high-density time-series
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Problem: High-frequency time-series (short-sampled telemetry and microsecond traces) are causing slow initial paint and massive DOM/Canvas churn. Screen reader users also get overwhelmed when every data point becomes an announcement during scrubbing or keyboard navigation. This ticket defines a design for: (1) a set of decimation profiles (aggressive, balanced, fidelity) that the rendering runtime can apply based on viewport/CPU/heurstic signals, and (2) a companion "announceable thresholds" surface that determines which aggregated events should produce sr-announcements and focus updates.
acceptance_criteria: Design artifact (Figma) showing three decimation profiles and the visual differences on a dense multi-series chart
Annotated UX flow for keyboard focus movement with 'announceable thresholds' and SR-friendly summaries
Token mapping for visual density (line-opacity, point-size, aggregation-badge) in the design system
Edge-case behaviour documented: how canary rollouts to low-powered devices will default to aggressive decimation
Performance targets: initial interactive paint < 1200ms for 10k points on mid-tier GPU when using balanced profile
Hand-off notes for engineering include pixel-mapped examples and accessibility phrasing for aria-live regions
design_notes: Introduce three named decimation profiles with explicit trade-offs: 'fidelity' (preserve peaks/valleys), 'balanced' (preserve trends), 'aggressive' (preserve overall envelope)

Expose a small config in the chart component props: decimationProfile: 'fidelity'|'balanced'|'aggressive' and announceThreshold: numeric percentage representing relative change to produce an SR announcement
Visual tokens: density-scale (1|2|3), point-visibility boolean, mini-aggregation-badge token and alpha values that live in the design tokens file

Keyboard UX: when focusing series or scrubbing, announcements should be grouped and rate-limited (max 1 announcement per 800ms) and summaries should be provided describing aggregated delta over viewport range
Screen reader phrasing: avoid full datum-by-datum readout. Use templates like 'Series X: stable trend; max 12% increase over last 5 minutes'
Legend interactions: hovering/clicking a legend item should toggle series and trigger a single summary announcement only when the visible envelope crosses announceThreshold
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: prefer aggregated announcements + summary over verbose per-point SR output to reduce cognitive load. Potential downside: loss of per-point granularity for users who require it. Mitigation: provide a 'detailed-read' toggle in Chart settings for assistive users.

Trade-off: aggressive decimation reduces visual noise but can hide short spikes. Chosen mitigation is to ensure 'fidelity' profile remains available and automatic profile selection leans conservative for anomaly-detection dashboards.
Decision: tokenizing density adjustments rather than ad-hoc inline styles so operations can be audited and toggled via theme (dark/light) and runtime capabilities
implementation_notes: Deliver UI tokens: density-scale-1/2/3, point-presence, aggregation-badge-size, series-alpha-decay. Add tokens to tokens/charts.json and document usage in the component README.
Figma file: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/decimation-profiles (WIP) — includes side-by-side renderings for 1k/10k/100k point scenarios
Engineering PR placeholder: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/PLACEHOLDER — will include storybook stories for each profile and an a11y storybook addon test
Compatibility: default prop remains 'balanced' to avoid regressions. Add runtime hints for Dedicated to override to 'aggressive' when capacity constraints are detected.
QA checklist: manual SR testing with NVDA and VoiceOver, automated Lighthouse checks for initial render time on throttled CPU, visual diffing for fidelity profile on synthetic traces
